newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: US fund selling sees NZ dlr finish near day's lows.
newsitem.headline: US fund selling sees NZ dlr finish near day's lows.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar ended near its session lows on Wednesday in a quiet session plagued by selling from U.S. fund managers.

At 5.30 p.m. (0530 GMT) the currency was quoted at US$0.6423/28, down from its 0.6450/57 open and 0.6443/50 finish on Tuesday. The kiwi traded a range of 0.6418-54 during the day. On its Trade-Weighted Index the kiwi dropped to 64.63 from 64.82 at the open and 64.55 at Tuesday's close.
Dealers said flows had calmed down from those seen in recent days, but selling pressure was quietly nibbling away at the kiwi's early gains.
"The selling is certainly being met by a lot of end-holders of kiwi and all the shorts are taking back their positions, but the market remains heavy," a Wellington dealer said.
"The best advice remains to sell any rally that occurs, because these American funds still seem intent on trying to get it down."
The kiwi was expected to open slightly lower on Thursday.
